name: UK inflation & rates
value: CPI 3.5% (Sep); Bank Rate 4%; Oct CPI 18 Nov
summary: Bank Rate 4% after 5 Nov rise; markets price over 80% chance of a December rise; October CPI due 18 Nov
state: UK CPI inflation was 3.5% in September, inside the 2.5–4.0% Watch band, and the Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise in more than three years. By 13 Nov LSEG data put the chance of a further rise in December above 80% (Trading Economics). Deutsche Bank expects October inflation to move higher (FXStreet, 11 Nov). The ONS publishes October CPI on 18 Nov; a print above 4% would cross the Alert line.
for_you: Higher Bank Rate feeds through to variable and tracker mortgages and new fixed deals, and to savings rates. Households with mortgages ending soon are most exposed to the change.
rubric_hit: Watch: CPI 3.5% (Sep) within 2.5–4.0% band; BoE reversed course with 5 Nov rise to 4%

why: UK inflation and the Bank Rate set mortgage, savings and business borrowing costs for the whole country.
drivers: Energy prices, wages, services inflation, sterling, global rates.

rubric.alert: CPI > 4.0%, or an emergency BoE move.
rubric.watch: CPI 2.5–4.0%, or the BoE reversing course.
rubric.normal: CPI ≤ 2.5% and Bank of England moving gradually or on hold.
